paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. You have not come to a mountain that scares everybody into begging for silence. You have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, to angels in joyful assembly, and to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant (Hebrews 12:22-24). That is a whole different kind of welcome, and it is yours.

So the writer says live like it. Pursue peace with everyone, as well as holiness, and watch out for each other so no one falls short of the grace of God (Hebrews 12:14-15). Esau gave up his birthright for a single meal (Hebrews 12:16), and that is what happens when we treat a big gift like a small snack. The sprinkled blood speaks a better word than the blood of Abel (Hebrews 12:24), so don't trade that word for anything.

And listen, because this is the part I want you to carry out of my bakery. "See to it that you do not refuse Him who speaks" (Hebrews 12:25). Everything that can be shaken will be removed, but we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, so let us be filled with gratitude and worship God "with reverence and awe" (Hebrews 12:27-28). I know what it is to be rattled around in the dark, baker, and I am telling you, THIS is the one thing that stays put!
